subject: pulse-oximeter
gradingContext: Orchestrator pixel grade at native 900x900 plus a 1:1 crop of the parting seam at box (420,430,680,690), against the #702 80k reference (tools/openclinxr/asset-pipeline/trellis/boxy-subject-bake-renders/pulse-oximeter-80k-reference.png) at the same box. The reference shows a smooth continuous groove with a soft shadow and no jagged content.
controlNote: THE CONTROL IS THE POINT (#703): all three cells bake the SAME 25,000-triangle low rung from the SAME 296,226-triangle source; bake resolution is the ONLY variable. Clause (2) refuses a ladder that re-decimates per cell. The 512 mapped GLB reproduces the #702 hand-run figure to the byte (8,682,420), so this is the same rung the graded champion was baked from.
resolutionEffect: CONFIRMED — bake resolution thins the streaks. 512 shows a broad ragged band, 1024 collapses it to a fine line, 2048 is marginally cleaner than 1024. The 512 default is wrong for a tight concavity. But the artifact never reaches absent at any resolution tried, so the map does not fully reproduce the reference seam even at 2048.
costCollapse: Raising resolution fixes the artifact and simultaneously destroys the reason to bake. Against the shipped 80k champion at 9,928,748 bytes: 512 is -12.6%, 1024 is -2.2%, 2048 is +27.0%. #702 measured this subject's BARE 25k rung at -23.7%. So a map clean enough to ship is worth 2.2% at best, against 23.7% for no map at all. On this subject the map's byte advantage was contingent on the resolution that produces the artifact.
recommendation: Do not raise the --bake-res default on this evidence. The honest reading is that a 512 map buys bytes and artifacts together, and a 1024 map buys neither. Whether texture compression (KTX2/basis) can hold 1024 quality at 512-like bytes is UNTESTED and is the lever that would change this verdict.
bakeStage: tools/openclinxr/asset-pipeline/trellis/iterate-optimize.ts --bake --bake-res <n> --target <25k low rung> (hl_bake.py high-to-low, export_mapped.py attach, ab_render.py grade PNG)

cells.verdictNote: Baseline cell, byte-identical to the #702 mapped rung. A broad ragged band of jagged light and dark runs the length of the parting seam where the reference has a smooth groove. Full-strength streaks; no reduction to measure against.
The ragged band collapses to a fine line. Most of the available improvement arrives here. Still not clean: a thin bright/dark line persists along the seam where the reference has none.
Marginally cleaner than 1024 and materially no better. The same thin seam line persists. Doubling resolution again bought almost nothing visually and cost 2.9 MB.

referenceRenders.note: The graded 80k shipped-champion reference render from #702, same renderer and framing — the known-good column for the parting-seam crop.

notEvidenceFor: that any resolution is adoptable — the orchestrator's grade records what each resolution does to the streaks and what it costs in bytes, and nothing here asserts a ready-to-ship claim
that the streaks are visible at learner viewing distance, which no capture has established
that bake resolution interacts with the low rung's triangle count — the ladder holds triangles fixed at 25,000, so it cannot see that interaction
that a resolution answer for pulse-oximeter transfers to the shoe
claimScope: a bake-resolution ladder exists on one fixed 25k low rung with three stage-written bake reports and three renders recorded at 512 / 1024 / 2048, graded by the orchestrator at a 1:1 parting-seam crop against the 80k reference; the renders are the oracle.
